claims.hypothesis: Millimeter RRLs (H40alpha) are reliable probes of electron density in UC HII regions and 3 mm continuum is dominated by free-free emission.
claims.experiment: Derive electron densities independently from H40alpha line luminosity and from 3 mm continuum emission across 94 UC HII regions and compare them.
claims.result: The two independent electron density measurements are strongly correlated with r = 0.97 (p << 0.001) and an xy-bisector slope of 0.95 +/- 0.01.
claims.finding: Millimeter RRLs are good probes of electron densities and 3 mm continuum emission in these UC HII regions is predominantly free-free emission.

evidence.loc: 3.2.4 Electron density derived from 3 mm radio continuum
evidence.quote: There is a strong correlation between these two measurements with a correlation coefficient of 0.97 and p-value ⌧ 0.001. The xy-bisector fit to these data gives a slope of 0.95 ± 0.01, indicating that millimeter RRLs are good probes of electron densities.

claims.hypothesis: The ionic abundance ratio Y+ (n_He+/n_H+) varies spatially within resolved UC HII regions.
claims.experiment: Compute pixel-by-pixel Y+ maps from He40alpha/H40alpha intensity ratios for 44 UC HII regions and compare Y+ distributions across H40alpha contour zones (80%-100% vs 20%-40% of peak) using a Kolmogorov-Smirnov test.
claims.result: Boundary regions show higher Y+ than central regions (KS test p << 0.001), with boundary He40alpha detections having S/N > 5.
claims.finding: Observed Y+ increases toward the boundaries of UC HII regions, not due to low S/N, possibly due to secondary ionization of He in the center or C40alpha line contamination near the PDR.

evidence.loc: 4.1 Variance of ionic abundance ratio (Y+) within UC Hii regions

claims.hypothesis: H40alpha line widths in UC HII regions are broadened by thermal and microturbulent/dynamical motions rather than electron pressure broadening.
claims.experiment: Calculate thermal and pressure broadening as functions of n_e and T_e following Peters et al. (2012), subtract thermal broadening to obtain microturbulent broadening Delta_V_tur, and correlate Delta_V_tur with effective radius R_eff.
claims.result: For n_e between 10^3 and 10^5 cm^-3, pressure broadening is negligible; Delta_V correlates with T_e (r = 0.49, p << 0.001) and Delta_V_tur anticorrelates weakly with R_eff (r = -0.22, p << 0.001).
claims.finding: Pressure broadening has no significant effect on H40alpha line widths; thermal motion and microturbulence dominate, with dynamical mechanisms contributing more in smaller (R_eff < 0.1 pc) UC HII regions.

evidence.quote: For the UC Hii regions in our ATOMS sources, n 4 are between 10 3 and 10 5 cm −3, and thus the pressure broadening has no significant effect on the spectral line widths.

claims.hypothesis: Electron temperature T_e of UC HII regions increases significantly with galactocentric distance R_GC as seen in single-dish HII region surveys.
claims.experiment: Derive non-LTE T_e for the sample from H40alpha-to-3mm continuum ratios and perform a linear fit of T_e against R_GC.
claims.result: Linear fit gives T_e = (6271 +/- 481) + (135 +/- 83) R_GC with r = 0.17, showing only a weak dependence on R_GC and systematically higher T_e than single-dish samples at the same R_GC.
claims.finding: Unlike previous single-dish studies of lower-density HII regions, T_e in this compact UC HII sample depends only weakly on R_GC, likely due to the narrow R_GC range (4-8 kpc) and higher collisional de-excitation of metal cooling lines in dense UC HII regions.

why_this_data.value: Submm/mm RRLs penetrate natal gas clumps of embedded UC HII regions, are much less affected by pressure broadening and brighter than cm RRLs, and ATOMS provides high angular resolution (~2.5 arcsec) to resolve UC HII regions unlike previous single-dish surveys.

evidence.quote: For young Ultra-Compact (UC) Hii regions that are still embedded in their natal gas clumps and are not visible at optical and infrared wavelengths, submm/mm RRLs are among the best tracers for probing their physical properties because they are much less affected by the pressure broadening, and brighter than the centimeter RRLs with larger principal quantum numbers (Keto et al. 2008).

In this work, we present the first systematic investigation of the properties of a large sample of resolved UC Hii regions with high resolution (⇠2.5 00 ) RRLs H40 U and He40 U as well as the 3mm continuum emission that was obtained from the ATOMS (ALMA Three-millimeter Observations of Massive Star forming regions) survey.

referee_caveats_inferred: C40alpha is separated from He40alpha by only ~9.05 MHz (~27.4 km/s at 99 GHz), which is comparable to the median line width of ~30 km/s; without multi-Gaussian deblending, C40alpha emission from the surrounding PDR can systematically inflate He40alpha integrated intensities at the HII region boundaries.
In Table 1, sources without He40alpha detections are listed with Y+ = 0.00 +/- 0.00 rather than upper limits or null values, which could mislead automated catalog reuse.
n_e(RRL) in Section 3.2.1 is computed assuming a fixed T_e = 10^4 K for the recombination efficiency eta, whereas the non-LTE T_e derived in Section 3.2.3 has a median of 6662 K.

Any residual thermal dust contribution to the 3 mm continuum will lower the line-to-continuum ratio and bias the derived T_e upward, which could partly explain why T_e is higher than in cm-wavelength single-dish surveys.
